text:
Maria Chen: Quick check — hit rate dropped from 0.87 -> 0.63 during the 12:05 spike. Suspect prefix-cache eviction threshold too aggressive. Can someone run a small sweep on prefix-cache eviction thresholds (0.5 / 0.6 / 0.65 / 0.7) and report kv.hit_rate, kv.evictions, kv.fragmentation, latency.p95? Thinking 0.65 might be sweet spot.

Rui Patel: On it. Spinning up kv_bench runs now. Using kv_bench v0.9, seed=42, 10k reqs each. Starting with 0.5. Command I run: 
```
./tools/kv_bench --runs 10000 --model=opt-1.3b --seq=1024 --prefix-evict=0.5 --emit-kv-metrics --sample-hotset
```
Will push raw logs to GCS when done.

deploy-bot: alert: prefixcache.eviction_rate spike detected at 2026-02-24T12:06Z (service=serve-prod, region=us-west1). Posted to thread.

Jordan Lee: Add --emit-fragmentation and --emit-occupancy flags to the bench. Also capture a quick perf profile during the middle of the run: `perf record -e cycles:u -g -- ./target/serve --port 9000` so we can see kernel hotspots if eviction logic is thrashing.

Matt O'Connor: Quick helper to compute mean occupancy from bench output: 
```bash
# occupancy.csv columns: ts,prefix_id,occupancy_bytes
awk -F, '{sum+=$3} END {print "mean_occupancy_bytes="sum/NR}' occupancy.csv
```
Also watch p95 latency and p99 for tail regressions.

Rui Patel: Results (single-run quick summary):
- prefix-evict=0.5 -> kv.hit_rate=0.59, kv.evictions=14000, kv.fragmentation=0.12, latency.p95=180ms
- prefix-evict=0.6 -> kv.hit_rate=0.70, kv.evictions=9000, kv.fragmentation=0.11, latency.p95=160ms
- prefix-evict=0.65 -> kv.hit_rate=0.75, kv.evictions=7200, kv.fragmentation=0.10, latency.p95=155ms
- prefix-evict=0.7 -> kv.hit_rate=0.76, kv.evictions=7000, kv.fragmentation=0.13, latency.p95=170ms
Notes: fragmentation metric didn't change much across runs; 0.7 increases tail slightly. Raw artifacts: gs://redwood-temp/kv/sweeps/1765432100/ (bench.log, occupancy.csv, perf.data)

Maria Chen: Good signal. Plan: canary default prefix-evict=0.65 for 6 hours at 5% traffic, monitor these metrics + application error rate. @Jordan Lee please add sampling traces and make sure trace ids propagate for the canary. I'll open a small PR to flip default behind a feature flag.

Jordan Lee: Will add sampling and a tracing tag `kv_canary=evict_0.65`. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/4123 (adds flag, test, canary rollout script).

sre-bot: scheduled canary rollout for prefix-evict=0.65 at 1765434600 (6% traffic window). Alerting rule: kv.hit_rate drop > 0.05 for 10m -> rollback.

Maria Chen: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short postmortem if anything funky shows up. :thumbsup:
